outcome: Bound the availability cost of the account-export surface (C3's second recorded gap). Per-client rate limits on the three export routes in owner_routes.py (request POST 10/hour, request-page GET 60/minute, status GET 60/minute, download proxy GET 30/hour), declared as a MappingProxyType there and applied in app.py after blueprint registration via the PLANNED_RATE_LIMITS idiom so declaration and application cannot drift; the request route serves GET and POST from one view, so entries carry (spec, methods) pairs. In services/account_export_storage_service.py read_final, the 100 MiB compressed cap moves BEFORE the archive download: the provider-reported size is refused when over the cap or disagreeing with the ledger's expected size, reusing the oversize_compressed and storage_size_mismatch codes; every existing post-read verification stays. The 429 stays the app's static content-free JSON sentence and never varies by whether a job exists. New tests pin exact mapping coverage, applied wiring, the 429 body, and both pre-read refusals with no byte downloaded. Retires the 'No rate limit on the download proxy' C3 bullet. No template, flag, schema, worker, or deployment change.
